dmitri: Quick thread — ran the KV-cache paging pressure sweep across regions and GPUs, posting raw notes here. TL;DR: H100 kernel selection improved p50 vs A100 on heavy-tail seqlen, but paging threshold tuning matters more for p99.
alice: Awesome, can you paste the exact sweep config?
dmitri: run_kv_bench --model redwood-13b-q4 --gpus [A100,H100] --regions [us-west,eu-central,ap-south] --seqlen-dist 'mix:90@512,8@2048,2@8192' --batch 8 --kv-page-size 256MB --eviction {lru,lfu,clock} --prefetch {on,off}
eva: Nice. What metrics did you capture?
dmitri: p50/p95/p99 latency, throughput (tokens/s), kv_hit_rate, paging_io_mb, gpu_util, selected_kernel
charlie: Any surprising regional diffs?
dmitri: Yes — us-west H100 runs with kernel Xv3 had p50 ~18% lower than A100 when kv_hit_rate >= 0.92. But p99 spikes align with paging_io > 120MB/s regardless of GPU.
alice: Can you share a tiny excerpt of the csv output?
dmitri: ```
#region,gpu,kernel,kv_hit,throughput_tok_s,p50_ms,p95_ms,p99_ms,paging_mb_s
us-west,A100,legacy,0.88,4200,22,85,220,150
us-west,H100,Xv3,0.93,4900,18,62,180,95
eu-central,H100,Xv3,0.91,4700,19,70,190,110
ap-south,A100,legacy,0.84,3600,28,120,340,210
``` 
eva: H100 Xv3 shows throughput uplift and tighter tails when kv_hit >= ~0.9. That suggests kernel benefits are amplified by hit-rate.
charlie: What about eviction strategy effect?
dmitri: LFU improved steady-state hit-rate for our mixed seqlen by ~2-3% vs LRU (same mem budget). That translated to 6-12% p95 improvement, p99 improvement only when paging_io stayed below ~100MB/s.
alice: Did you try lowering page size?
dmitri: Yes — 128MB pages reduced tail IO bursts, p99 dropped ~15% in worst regions but hit-rate fell ~1%. Trade-off looks worth it for latency-sensitive customers.
kv-bench-bot: Automated summary: H100+Xv3 best p50/p95 for heavy-tail workloads when kv_hit >= 0.9; tune eviction->LFU and page_size->128MB to reduce p99. See /data/kv-bench/1790123456/*.csv
eva: Any capacity-sizing rule-of-thumb from this sweep?
dmitri: For mixed workloads: reserve GPU capacity ~20% above steady tokens/s target if average seqlen >512 and allow burst headroom for region with worst paging_io. If hit-rate <0.85, either increase memory (reduce miss rate) or add GPUs to reduce per-GPU pressure.
charlie: Kernel fallback behavior — was there any automatic fallback causing variance?
dmitri: Yes, we saw the routing layer sometimes fallback to kernel legacy on H100 when sequence-lengths frequently exceeded the per-invocation compile cache window; adding kernel warming (keep-alive compile) eliminated that variance.
alice: Anything for the ops playbook? short bullets please.
dmitri: - Prefer H100+Xv3 for latency-sensitive deployments with heavy-tail seqlen distributions. - Configure eviction=LFU and page_size=128MB for better tails. - Monitor kv_hit_rate and paging_io_mb, set alert if p99 > 2*slo or paging_io > 100MB/s. - Pre-warm kernels on new instances to avoid fallback jitter.
eva: Thanks — can we add a small figure for internal doc? even an ASCII sparkline is fine.
dmitri: p99_us-west_H100: 180 190 95  (before/after page_size and eviction) -> sparkline: ▇▆▁
charlie: I'll add these notes to the KB and run a longer 72h run focused on ap-south.
dmitri: Yea please. I'll push the full CSVs and run configs to the bench bucket and tag the PR.
